item.description: Trainers check on Texas edge Colin Simmons (1) after an injury during the game against Florida at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Texas football could soon get its best defensive player back on the field after a one-game absence. Colin Simmons , the SEC's sack leader this season, missed Texas' 34-27 win over Ole Miss on Saturday due to a right-ankle sprain . The injury may only keep him sidelined one week, as Simmons was listed as questionable on Wednesday's availability report for Texas' upcoming game against Mississippi State. Simmons' potential return is welcome news for Texas' defense. The Longhorns also received positive injury news Wednesday regarding three offensive players. Running back Hollywood Smothers is probable for Saturday night's matchup after missing the Ole Miss game due to a shoulder injury. Wide receivers Kaliq Lockett and Cam Coleman are also probable. Lockett didn't play against Ole Miss, while Coleman exited the Ole Miss game due to a shoulder injury in the third quarter. Goosby was carted off the field in last week's win over Ole Miss due to a left-knee injury in the first quarter, and he did not return to the game. Tennessee has bolstered its 2027 recruiting class by securing a commitment from three-star cornerback Preston Glasco on Wednesday evening, beating out Alabama and Georgia for the Grayson High School standout. The 6-foot-2, approximately 190-pound prospect had previously committed to UConn on June 10 but reopened his recruitment on September 22. The Volunteers extended a scholarship offer on September 24 and quickly emerged as a contender despite entering the race later than the Crimson Tide and Bulldogs. Alabama offered Glasco in September and gained momentum, while Georgia remained involved throughout the process. Glasco also completed official visits to both programs, visiting the Bulldogs in June and the Crimson Tide in late September. Tennessee made its move after hosting him for the Volunteers’ October 17 game against Alabama in Knoxville. That visit gave the coaching staff an opportunity to make its case before Glasco reached his decision. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Head coach Josh Heupel’s relationship with the defensive back also contributed to the Volunteers recruitment. Glasco described the head coach as approachable and said his experience with Heupel had matched his expectations since receiving the offer. Defensive coordinator Jim Knowles and Coach Jones also helped improve Tennessee’s position. Glasco’s physical profile makes him a developmental prospect with potential at cornerback. He possesses long limbs, quick footwork and the reach to challenge receivers at the catch point. He also demonstrates physicality against the run and works to disrupt receivers’ timing in coverage. However, Glasco still needs to improve his ability to locate the football and develop his deep speed. Injuries limited his playing time during much of his sophomore and junior seasons, potentially affecting his recruiting rankings. He reportedly made major progress early in his senior campaign. His evaluations vary across recruiting services. The 247Sports Composite lists Glasco as the No. 88 cornerback in the 2027 class, while another 247Sports ranking places him at No. 69 nationally among cornerbacks. He is also ranked among Georgia’s top 104 players in the cycle. Glasco becomes the Volunteers’ 19th commitment in the 2027 recruiting class, and their sixth defensive back. Tennessee ranks No. 22 nationally in the 247Sports team rankings. The class includes five-star running back David Gabriel Georges, alongside four-star prospects such as tight end Malik Howard, wide receiver KeSean Bowman, linebacker Kenneth Simon and offensive tackle Princeton Uwaifo. item.title: Clay County volleyball duo reaches final four. What about Beachside?
item.description: Beachside knew Wednesday night would make Jacksonville-area volleyball history. Even if the ultimate result was out of their hands. "They're going to take pride in competing at a high level and playing well, so all the other stuff is really ancillary," Beachside coach Austin Lanteigne said. "We can't really control that." In the first-ever Florida High School Athletic Association Open Division match in any sport to be played in Northeast Florida, Beachside did what it needed to do by beating Naples First Baptist 25-17, 25-19, 23-25, 25-18. The FHSAA's complicated tiebreaker scenario, however, kept the Oct. 28 match from feeling like a total victory. Watch Florida high school sports live on NFHS Network Got a great play? How to submit your high school sports highlights to the Times-Union Despite winning two of three matches in the FHSAA's inaugural super division , containing the eight highest-ranked programs in the association's rating system, Beachside (26-4) appeared set to finish behind Clearwater Calvary Christian and Tampa Plant for the two state semifinal spots from the four-team round-robin Pool B. The Barracudas' problem: Beachside beat Calvary Christian on Oct. 21, Plant beat Beachside on Oct. 24, and in the other pool match Wednesday, Calvary Christian beat Plant. Had Plant defeated Calvary Christian, Beachside would have progressed automatically in second place. Instead, all three ended 2-1, and the FHSAA's tiebreaking criterion — total points allowed during the Open Division — looked set to leave the Barracudas out of the finals in Winter Haven. Calvary Christian allowed 237 points in three matches, fewest among the trio, which under the formula would bring first place. Then, under the FHSAA's most recently published tiebreaker — a topic that has been at the center of considerable confusion during the past week — Plant would edge out Beachside for second based on head-to-head. The FHSAA has not yet posted an updated bracket or otherwise announced a resolution to the tiebreaker as of Wednesday night. Whatever the FHSAA's number-crunching, Beachside played like championship contenders for most of the way Wednesday. Rallying from an early 8-3 deficit, Beachside uncorked a 10-1 run behind freshman Nina Simanic to win the first. Middle blocker Leanna Deutou then turned around the second with a key block for a two-set edge. After Maggie Adamczyk and McKinley Bright punished several third-set errors and brought the Lions (25-5) back to win the third, Beachside finished off the fourth with more clutch kills from Nina Simanic and Mollie VanDeusen. If Wednesday was the end of Beachside's road, it closes the outstanding high school careers of a six-strong senior class — VanDeusen, Deutou, Vinessa Rafael, Isabella Taveras Seda, Lillian Jimenez and Maya Bell — that helped put Barracuda volleyball on the statewide map. item.title: Red Wings Thinking Less, Applying More
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Red Wings have managed to avoid what should have been a disastrous start to their season considering the offseason headlines nipping at the team’s heels. The Red Wings have for the most part been able to answer the bell, weathering the dark clouds of Dylan Larkin’ s trade request and the absence of Simon Edvinsson still hanging over the franchise as October draws to a close. Making things work There’s been a considerable amount of change in the Red Wings lineup, due in part to those storylines, and in other cases, because the players are making their own. Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard have been able to bring a considerable amount of youthful punch to the team’s forward corps, and look to be perhaps more important factors in the team’s future than many had considered, even with high expectations going into the year. The Red Wings are seeing steady improvements from around the roster, and while patience for the team’s rebuild has long run out, the fruits of the Yzerplan’s labor are finally beginning to drop, even without the architect behind it pulling the strings. Instead, the team has had to rely on itself. As the month has gone on, Detroit has seemed to find its footing despite a slow start in Hockeytown. After losing four of their first five games, the Red Wings have clawed back to a 5-4-3 record, with two games left to play in October. “The structure that we’re playing with, we’re seeing improvements day after day. It’s becoming- less thought about and more just applied, which is good.” Said head coach Todd McLellan. McLellan changed some of the team’s operating structures in the offseason, and it looks like his team is liking the adjustments. Recipes For Detroit, success is still only just being found in razor thin margins. Detroit has scored a game-tying goal in the final two minutes of regulation a league-leading three games so far this season. Three of the Red Wings’ four wins have been decided by one goal. On the flip side, three of their losses have been decided by a margin of 2+ goals. The Red Wings have for the most part been able to keep games tight, but when things unravel, the Red Wings don’t have many answers. In games where the Red Wings are trailing after two periods, they have a record of 1-4-2 on the year, and have lost as many 1-goal games in overtime as they’ve won. “I think obviously a couple games and you’re out of the playoffs pretty fast. A couple wins in a row and you’re right back in it,” Mo Seider said, “I think we just kind of get some traction. Obviously don’t want to be in those games all season long, those tight ones, and hopefully come up with big points.” In a Red Wings season where the franchise seems set to lose their former captain, and, worst case, a top pairing defenseman as well, Hockeytown can use all the wins they can get. Also out are tight end Shane King and defensive linemen Kevin Moore and Ezra Funa , the latter having not played yet this season. Cole had started the first seven games this season, allowing only 16 catches on 30 targets, and is among the top-graded corners in the Big 12. In his absence the UA is likely to start Dwight Bootle II, who has been part of a 3-man rotation at the two corner spots with Cole and Tyrese Boss. Slot DB Malcolm Hartzog Jr. could also see time at corner. On the offensive side, receivers Chris Hunter and Giovanni Richardson are listed as questionable. Both have missed the past two games after getting hurt Oct. 3 vs. Cincinnati, the same game fellow WR Tre Spivey suffered a season-ending injury. Tight end Cole Rusk , who has been out several games, is listed as doubtful. Also listed as questionable are running back Ismail Mahdi and linebacker Max Harris but not because of injury. item.title: From Startup to State Bound: Legacy sweeps Lourdes for first region title
item.description: PORT ST. LUCIE — Unlike most movies and music albums, the Legacy High School volleyball team proved that sequels can be better than the original. The Lions were incredibly impressive in their debut season in 2025, winning a district title and reaching the regional finals in their first year of existence. The crowning moment of their encore performance in 2026 resulted in a near-sonic boom of applause and, more importantly, has them bound for Central Florida. Second-year Legacy earned its first state tournament appearance after defeating Lourdes Academy in three sets during the Region 4-4A final Wednesday in front of a raucous crowd inside the Legacy High School gymnasium. Set scores were 25-16, 25-19 and 25-21 in favor of the Lions, who will play in a Class 4A state semifinal next week. “I really can’t put it into words,” Legacy coach Christy Quigley said. “It really feels amazing, but amazing just doesn’t seem like a good enough word for it.” Startup program to back-to-back: Legacy volleyball makes more district history More: St. Edward’s returns to states, outlasts Brevard HEAT in Region Final As loud as the gym was following match point, Legacy's players were just as amped up between the second and third sets. They walked toward the entrance of their locker room and could be heard over music from the DJ booth blaring through the speakers. However, all of that noise quieted once the Bobcats (20-9) used a 6-0 run to build a 10-5 lead in the third set, prompting a Quigley timeout. The message in the huddle was direct. “We had to calm down and play our game,” senior right-side hitter Sophia Spychalla said. “We know what we’re doing. We just have to focus on our serves and our passing, and we’ll be good.” The hosts quickly climbed back into it. Two kills from senior outside hitter Taylor Smith kick-started a 6-1 run that put the Lions (24-7) ahead 14-13. The third set was a back-and-forth battle from there. The teams were tied six times before Legacy made a 5-0 push to secure the regional championship. A Smith kill, followed by an ace from sophomore defensive specialist Isabella Gago and a kill from senior setter Meredith Prince, put the Lions on the brink. Then, on match point, Lourdes senior Sierra Cotter hit an attack out of bounds in front of the Lions’ bench to start the celebration. “I’m literally shaking right now. I honestly don’t know what to feel,” Smith said. “I’m so proud of everyone on my team. We went to the regional finals last year, and we got to come back and prove ourselves this year. Now, I want to go farther and win the state championship.” Legacy was the No. 1 seed in Region 4-4A, while the Bobcats were the No. 2 seed. The Lions have won their last seven matches. The Class 4A state semifinals will take place next Wednesday at the Winter Haven Health Center at Polk State College in Winter Haven. item.title: SF Giants owner Charles B. Johnson outspending rest of MLB combined in midterm donations this cycle
item.description: The San Francisco Giants logo is seen on a jersey during the game between the Boston Red Sox and the San Francisco Giants at Fenway Park on Aug. 22, 2026, in Boston. (Winslow Townson/Getty Images) San Francisco Giants owner Charles Johnson spent more money on this year's midterms than all other MLB owners combined, with a majority going to Republican candidates and organizations. Front Office Sports published a series on Wednesday highlighting the amount of money the sports world has spent on the upcoming 2026 elections. Johnson was among the highest spenders not just in the baseball world but among sports owners as a whole. with an estimated $2.6 million in donations this cycle. As FOS notes in its report, MLB owners as a whole donated a little more than $4 million, making Johnson's money a majority of political spending throughout the league. Johnson is also fourth in federal donations among all majority owners of NFL, NBA, WNBA, NHL, MLB, NWSL and MLS teams. The only three ahead of him are Hawks owner Tony Ressler ($2.71 million spent), Broncos owner Rob Walton ($8.96 million) and Mavericks owner Miriam Adelson ($67.63 million). Johnson's Federal Election Commission filings reveal that the owner's money solely went to Republican causes. item.title: The best Kentucky Basketball starting lineup became obvious in win vs. UCF
item.description: Everyone knew Milan Momcilovic would be the star of this Kentucky Basketball team, and Malachi Moreno would be a huge piece. Three exhibition games later, that remains true. However, the best starting lineup Kentucky can put on the floor has definitely changed. After three games, Kentucky clearly has a lineup that will be the best group to have on the floor together, at least early on in the 2026-27 college basketball season. Point Guard: Mason Williams Writing about a player struggling is never fun. But the fact is Mason Williams is simply outplaying Zoom Diallo in nearly every aspect. Williams should be starting. Over three games, he averaged eight points, one rebound, one assist, and one steal per game. More importantly, he averaged under one turnover per game and controls the offense much better. Presumed starter Diallo has struggled. He averages just four points, two rebounds, two assists, and two turnovers a night. If he is not going to score at a high rate, those turnovers are just too difficult to overcome. After Diallo played more minutes in the season opener, the freshman Williams has seen his playing time surpass Diallo in consecutive games. I don’t think that stops. Shooting Guard: Alex Wilkins Posting a +32 plus-minus through three games, Wilkins is the kind of player who can get hot at any time. Turnovers are still an issue for him. However, his scoring offsets those mistakes when paired with the ability Williams has to protect the basketball. If Wilkins gets his turnovers under control, he will be a great piece going forward. Diallo could also be a nice change of pace player behind Wilkins, which is another reason Williams should be the starting point guard. Small Forward: Milan Momcilovic This does not require a long explanation. He is simply the best basketball player on this roster. He does everything well. He took over early in the overtime period against UCF by making three of the six total shots the team took. Power Forward: Ousmane N’Diaye This is probably the closest position battle on the roster. Justin McBride has looked really good at times, but N’Diaye gets the nod due to his ability to grab loose balls and defend multiple positions. His shooting needs to improve since he is shooting just 31% across three games. If he can consistently put the ball in the basket, he is definitely the starter. But for now it is a close battle, and N’Diaye’s upside gives him the nod. When Kam Williams returns, I may slot Williams at the 3 and push Milan up to the 4 here. Center: Malachi Moreno Moreno has all the physical tools you want from a big man, and he proved it by coming just two assists shy of a triple-double against UCF. He still needs to develop a nasty streak. If he ever gets aggressive, he will be unstoppable. That is exactly why Franck Kepnang provides such a nice foil off the bench. Kepnang is an uber-aggressive center who can spell Moreno. If Moreno picks up on that aggressive energy, he will become a very dangerous player.

item.title: Pirates Warned Against Making Potential Offseason Mistake
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates have a pivotal offseason ahead after finishing with an 82-80 record in the 2026 season. The Pirates were within six games of a National League Wild Card spot. Pittsburgh's 11-year playoff drought hangs over them, but they have some quality talent on the roster. If the Pirates have a strong offseason, they could make it into the postseason in the 2027 season. However, they need to avoid an ill-advised signing that limits their flexibility to upgrade the roster in the future. One player that Sports Illustrated urged Pittsburgh not to sign in free agency is second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. Chisholm is a two-time All-Star, but had a down year in the 2026 season with the New York Yankees . He slashed .231/.312/.399 with 19 home runs, 16 doubles, 41 stolen bases, 55 RBIs, and a .711 OPS. The 28-year-old has the versatility to play in the outfield or at third base as well, but the Pirates should avoid signing him. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Pittsburgh has another second baseman they should prioritize in free agency, as Brandon Lowe will be a free agent. The Pirates acquired Lowe ahead of the 2026 season, and he was their best hitter, slashing .260/.331/.493 with 35 home runs, 29 doubles, 96 RBIs, 94 runs, and an .824 OPS. Lowe has proven to be a quality power bat in Pittsburgh's lineup, and signing him to a new deal makes more sense for the Pirates than pursuing Chisholm. Chisholm could emerge as an option for Pittsburgh if they fail to re-sign Lowe, due to their previous interest in him at the 2024 trade deadline. Across his seven-year career, Chisholm is slashing .245/.315/.444 with 127 home runs, 95 doubles, 19 triples, 171 stolen bases, 363 RBIs, 385 runs, and a .759 OPS. He is a solid hitter, but would be pricey to acquire, when it makes more sense to lock up Lowe on a new deal. Aside from addressing the second base position, the Pirates need to add more to their lineup. They have a great young piece at shortstop in Konnor Griffin, who showed flashes as a rookie, slashing .272/.324/.404 with six home runs, 15 doubles, four triples, 23 stolen bases, 33 RBIs, 43 runs, and a .728 OPS. Pittsburgh needs to continue adding pieces to the lineup around Griffin, but Chisholm should not be one of those targets for the Pirates to make the jump to a playoff team in 2027.

item.title: From DeSoto Speedway to CARS Tour: The Freedom Factory’s Return to Short Track Racing
item.description: Bigley Tune Up Freedom Factory. Photo: Jordan Ashley White A Florida short track that once sat closed is preparing to host one of the country’s most recognizable Late Model racing tours. The Freedom Factory in Bradenton, formerly known as DeSoto Speedway, will host the zMAX CARS Tour’s 2027 season opener on February 6. It marks the series’ first visit to Florida and the latest step in the facility’s return to traditional short-track competition. DeSoto Speedway previously hosted regional and national touring series, including the ASA National Tour and NASCAR Southeast Series. Financial difficulties eventually forced the facility to close in 2018 before automotive YouTuber Cleetus McFarland purchased it in 2020. McFarland initially focused on automotive entertainment, building events around Ford Crown Victorias, burnouts, and other unconventional competitions. But traditional stock car racing has gradually returned, including the Bill Bigley Sr. Memorial 128 and UARA Super Late Model events. The CARS Tour announcement represents another step in that transition. Both the Late Model Stock Car and Pro Late Model divisions will compete on the three-eighths-mile asphalt oval, with Dale Earnhardt Jr., Kevin Harvick, and McFarland among the drivers expected to participate. The event also takes the CARS Tour farther south than ever before, expanding its reach beyond its traditional southeastern racing markets. At a time when other short tracks are struggling with operating costs and uncertain futures, the Freedom Factory offers an example of how a historic facility can find new uses while bringing competitive racing back to its original surface. The CARS Tour season opener is scheduled for February 6, 2027, with coverage on FloRacing.

item.title: Alabama cuts ties with defensive back after latest arrest
item.description: Dec 4, 2015; Atlanta, GA, USA; The Alabama Crimson Tide logo on the playing field at the Georgia Dome in preparation for the SEC Championship Saturday. Mandatory Credit: John David Mercer-USA TODAY Sports The Alabama Crimson Tide faces new controversy as a player has been charged with allegedly harassing a police officer online. As the Tide prepared for their matchup against the Texas A&M Aggies, defensive back Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. watched from home after being suspended. However, on Monday, head coach Kalen DeBoer told reporters that Kirkpatrick Jr. was “not with us,” and the program has since cut ties with him amid his pending criminal charges. Kirkpatrick Jr. was charged with harassing communications and doxing, both misdemeanors. DeBoer released a statement on Tuesday announcing the split. “After gathering more information on the situation, Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. will no longer be a part of our program,” DeBoer said in a statement, via ESPN . “He did not live up to the standards and expectations that I have set for this team and our players.” Kirkpatrick Jr. allegedly sent the officer a profane message that included, “text me back don’t be no b—-!” according to documents obtained by WBRC and The Tuscaloosa Thread. Kirkpatrick allegedly posted a photo of the officer and his family to his Facebook page with the caption, “Dis him?” which caused “severe concern for the overall safety and well-being of himself and his family,” given Kirkpatrick’s “substantial audience and public following” as an Alabama football player, the officer claimed in a criminal complaint, according to TMZ . Kirkpatrick Jr. was arrested last year on three counts of reckless endangerment and one count of attempting to elude and speeding, and he was suspended for the remainder of the 2025 season. The officer he allegedly targeted was involved in that arrest. Kirkpatrick appeared in Alabama’s first seven games of the 2026 season, recording four tackles before his departure. The Kirkpatrick name has rung bells around campus before, as his father, Dre Kirkpatrick, played for the Crimson Tide from 2009 to 2011 and won two national titles.
